name: MiniMax Music 3 (audio.cpp)
description: Lyrics-conditioned text-to-music. Unlike every other entry here it loads a package, not one GGUF: --model takes the weights directory and audio.cpp resolves five components (condition encoder, language model, flow transformer, RVQ depth decoder, vocoder) plus tokenizer/config JSON from it. The component filenames are not ours to choose - the loader resolves them from the package spec compiled into the binary and checks they exist before parsing any option, so neither --session-option nor --load-option can redirect them. This entry mirrors audio.cpp 0.6.1's minimax_music3_q4_0 package exactly, including its mixed quantisation: q4_0 language model and transformer, q8_0 RVQ depth decoder. Defaults are the loader's own published values.

name: ACE-Step 1.5 Base (audio.cpp)
description: Non-distilled sibling of the listed ACE-Step 1.5 Turbo: same ace_step loader, same GGUF repo, the base fine-tune instead of the few-step distillation. The shared ace_step advanced-params row caps num_inference_steps at 20, but that ceiling is the turbo's; the main Steps field passes through unclamped. Untested end-to-end through this adapter.

license.name: MIT License
license.note: MIT, same as the other ACE-Step 1.5 checkpoints. The card states the training data was licensed, public-domain or synthetic; that is a claim on the card, not a licence term.

name: HTDemucs 6-stem separation (audio.cpp)
description: Six-stem sibling of the HTDemucs entry: vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano and other. Run it from a sound's "Split into stems" action. Tiny download (42 MB). Run end to end on audio.cpp 0.9.2 (RTX 5080, CUDA): an 8.3 s song split in 18.8 s using about 1 GB of VRAM. As with the 4-stem model, a stem the mix does not contain comes out as loud, flat noise once Soundbox normalises it. Needs audio.cpp 0.9.2 or newer: older binaries do not have this loader.

license.name: MIT (code) / research-only (weights)
license.note: Same position as the 4-stem HTDemucs entry. The repository is MIT, but Demucs' maintainer has said the pretrained weights are not covered by it and are provided for scientific purposes only. audio.cpp's own licence table and the GGUF repo label this MIT; the weights are what you run, so it is treated here as non-commercial.

name: Kokoro 82M (audio.cpp)
description: Small, fast text-to-speech with 54 preset voices across English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese and Chinese. No cloning. Needs eSpeak-ng installed separately: audio.cpp phonemises through the eSpeak-ng shared library and the release does not include it, so without it every request fails with "Could not load eSpeak-ng". Needs audio.cpp 0.9.2 or newer: older binaries do not have this loader.

license.name: Apache License 2.0

name: Chatterbox Turbo (audio.cpp)

Output carries Resemble's Perth watermark. Run end to end on audio.cpp 0.9.2 (RTX 5080, CUDA): a one-sentence line in 5.5 s cold and 1.4 s warm, using about 1.8 GB of VRAM. Needs audio.cpp 0.9.2 or newer: older binaries do not have this loader.
